Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables with the joint probability density function 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & (x,y)\in D, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(-\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables with the joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

Let's draw the point $(-\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{2})$ on our diagram. Let's also consider the region $Δ$ that lies below and to the left of this point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274884/assets/72ec33b41b4a7d924cec49ca1d55856c36c56cec4db1e7c347eefc06cbe2d2f2.png)

Using the definition of the joint CDF, we have

$$
F(-\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{2})=P(X<-\frac{1}{4},Y<\frac{1}{2})={\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1/4}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

However, $f(u,v)$ is zero everywhere inside the region $Δ.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1/4}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v=0.\end{aligned}
$$
